example.heading: Illustration
example.text: Suppose an educational institution uses a campaign activity to combine yoga, self-defence demonstrations and a discussion on substance-abuse risks. The illustration shows how one platform could connect physical well-being, personal safety and awareness; it does not claim that such an event occurred.

pocketRead.excerpt: MY Bharat and NSS used Yoga evam Aatm-Suraksha Diwas to connect youth fitness, self-defence and substance-abuse awareness in the campaign’s second month.

question.answer: It can help by building healthy routines, confidence, stress-management awareness and community dialogue. However, awareness must be connected with counselling, rehabilitation and other public-health services; the supplied source does not establish such linkages.
question.prompt: How can combining fitness, self-defence and awareness support substance-abuse prevention, and what limitation should policymakers recognise?

sections.heading: An integrated preventive approach
paragraphs: MY Bharat and NSS launched Month 2 of the campaign through Yoga evam Aatm-Suraksha Diwas. The approach links physical activity, self-defence and awareness rather than treating substance-abuse prevention as information dissemination alone.

The mechanism is preventive: regular fitness and relaxation practices may support healthy routines and stress management, while self-defence activities can strengthen practical safety awareness and confidence. These are analytical mechanisms, not outcomes verified by the source.

sections.heading: Participation, inclusion and limits
paragraphs: The official summary records participation across educational institutions, NSS units and adopted villages, with local leaders, police officials, sports authorities, medical experts and certified yoga instructors involved. It also records women’s participation as 57.1% of total participation.

The source does not establish whether the activities changed substance-use behaviour or connected participants to treatment. Therefore, the campaign should be assessed not only by attendance and outreach, but also by referral, counselling and longer-term outcomes.

The supplied record does not provide an independently verified statutory definition of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan.
use: In GS2 answers, use the item to illustrate preventive public-health governance, youth mobilisation, women’s participation and the need to connect awareness with counselling and rehabilitation.

advisory_notes: “Static topic / anchor” is broadly appropriate under GS2 social-sector health and welfare, but the item is better framed as a government intervention than as a welfare scheme whose performance is being evaluated.
“GS1.5” is defensible only as a secondary society linkage through women’s participation and empowerment; the note should avoid presenting it as the primary syllabus fit.
“ESSAY.B” is an internal/editorial code rather than an official UPSC syllabus category; retain it only if the note system defines that code.
“preventive public-health governance” is a reasonable analytical inference, but the source reports activities and participation, not demonstrated public-health outcomes.
“Women’s participation” is source-supported, while claims that self-defence supports confidence or personal safety are mechanisms or intended effects, not measured outcomes.

The pocketRead headline and deck accurately summarise the source at a broad level, but “tools for addiction prevention” should be read as an analytical framing rather than an established impact finding.

The paragraph stating that institutions, NSS units, adopted villages, and listed stakeholders participated is supported by the downloaded extract [P1], but not by the supplied title-level official summary alone.

The arithmetic is sound: 34,290 + 31,507 + 25,391 = 91,188 activity-participations, which need not equal 91,179 unique participants because activities can overlap; the note appropriately avoids asserting equivalence.

wayForward: Link campaign activities with confidential counselling, early screening, referral and rehabilitation services.
Measure outcomes beyond attendance, including sustained participation, help-seeking, referrals and behavioural change.
Use schools, colleges, NSS units and adopted villages for locally adapted, multilingual communication.
Maintain coordination among youth institutions, health professionals, community organisations and relevant enforcement agencies.
